issues.body:
`_RAW_STRLIT_MASK_RE = (?<![A-Za-z0-9_"\\'])(?:br|r)(?P<hashes>#{0,255})"[\s\S]*?"(?P=hashes)`.

The widened lookbehind fixes the specific round-2 trigger (`"\r"`, `"...r"` after an alnum, `'r'`), and `test_escaped_cr_does_not_mask_following_live_cfg` genuinely pins it (I confirmed it returns `[]` under the round-2 regex and the correct expression under the new one). But the lookbehind still admits every OTHER character, so an `r` that is the last char of an ordinary literal preceded by a space, `/`, `-`, `.`, `:` etc. is read as a zero-hash raw-string opener, and `[\s\S]*?` consumes to the next `"` anywhere in the file. Raw masking runs first, so nothing corrects it.

Reproduced against the PR head:
  `let m = "mode r";\n#[cfg(not(feature = "quoted-triples"))]\nfn g() {}\n` -> `_extract_cfg_expressions()` returns `[]`
  `let m = "w/r";\n#[cfg(not(feature = "quoted-triples"))]\nfn g() {}\n`   -> `[]`
  `#[cfg(feature = "vector-r")]\nfn a() {}\n#[cfg(not(feature = "quoted-triples"))]\nfn g() {}\n`
     -> `['feature = "vector-r")]\nfn a() {}\n#[cfg(not(feature = "quoted-triples"']`  (one mangled expr; the second cfg is gone)

A left-to-right Rust lexer over `crates/**/*.rs` finds 86 spans where the matched `r"` is really the tail of an ordinary literal — the SAME count round 2 measured, i.e. the fix changed WHICH triggers fire, not HOW MANY. Verified by eye: `crates/sparq-fedplan/src/adaptive.rs:1542` `.predicate(pred("http://ex/r", 500, 500, 500))`.

Severity is major, not blocker, because I measured the blast radius: 0 of the 86 spans currently overlap a live `#[cfg(`, and `cmd_enforce` over all 169 legs returns 0 violations under both the old and new sanitizer. Nothing is mis-gated today. But the module docstring's core promise — "a detector bug degrades to 'keep the full leg', never to a silent demotion" — is still false, and the tree this scans changes every PR.
issues.fix_hint:
Stop widening the lookbehind — it is whack-a-mole: round 2 excluded `"\\'` and the false-opener count did not move. Replace both regexes with a single left-to-right character scanner that walks the file once tracking a state in {code, line comment, block comment, char literal, ordinary literal, raw literal with N hashes} and blanks the non-code spans in place (preserving length and CR/LF, which the existing `len(safe) == len(content)` assert already requires). That is ~40 lines, removes all three documented carve-outs (multi-line ordinary literals, `/* */` block comments, phantom raw openers) at once, and makes the docstring's invariant actually true.

If a full scanner is out of scope for this PR, the honest interim is to make the failure direction match the claim: when the raw mask and the ordinary mask disagree about a span, keep the span LIVE (fail closed — a spurious cfg only retains a leg) rather than masking it.

Either way add the two repros above as tests, plus a tree-level invariant test asserting that for every `crates/**/*.rs` file the sanitizer never reduces the number of extracted cfg expressions relative to a scan of the un-sanitized content restricted to real code.
issues.title: Raw-string mask still fails OPEN: any non-word char before a trailing `r` opens a phantom raw string and erases live cfg attributes

issues.body:
The fixture was changed from `"foo"` to `"feature-ending-in-r"`, which reads as coverage for the `-r"` phantom-opener hazard. It is not. I ran the fixture through both the round-2 regex and the round-3 regex:

  round2(old): ['feature = "feature-ending-in-r"']
  round3(new): ['feature = "feature-ending-in-r"']

Identical. It cannot fail on the defect it gestures at, because the fixture contains no `"` after the cfg for the lazy `[\s\S]*?` to reach, so the phantom opener finds no terminator and simply does not match. The change is also outside the stated intent of the fix (`-` is not in the new lookbehind class), and the real hazard IS live: add one more quoted line after the attribute and the extraction mangles, as shown in the major finding.
issues.fix_hint:
Either revert the fixture to `"foo"` (the test's job is the basic extraction path, which is already covered), or make it non-vacuous by appending a second attribute so the phantom opener has a terminator to reach:

  content = '#[cfg(feature = "vector-r")]\nfn a() {}\n#[cfg(not(feature = "quoted-triples"))]\nfn g() {}\n'
  self.assertEqual(det._extract_cfg_expressions(content),
                   ['feature = "vector-r"', 'not(feature = "quoted-triples")'])

That form goes red on the current code, which is the point.
issues.title: `test_extract_single_cfg` fixture change to `"feature-ending-in-r"` is vacuous — identical result under the pre-fix regex

issues.body:
The new §9.1 states: "The detector mutation demonstration remains pinned in `TestMutationCheck`". `grep -n '^class ' scripts/tests/test_feature_matrix_tiers.py` lists 13 classes and `TestMutationCheck` is not among them. The mutation demo actually lives in `TestMutationFailOpen` (line 574), whose divergence assertion is `test_mutation_check_divergence` (line 602).

This matters more than a typo would, because §9.1 is the PR's audit-evidence record for bead sq-s5dvo — the deliverable round 2 asked for. A dated record that points at a non-existent symbol is not verifiable evidence, and the next reader who greps for it will conclude the demo is missing.
issues.fix_hint: Change `TestMutationCheck` to `TestMutationFailOpen` (or cite `TestMutationFailOpen::test_mutation_check_divergence` in full, which is likely where the name came from). While there, check the sibling claim in the same paragraph — "the tier-enforcement tests additionally make a sensitive `tier: check` leg fail invariant (1)" — which does check out: `TestEnforceMode::test_check_tier_sensitive_fails` at line 454.
issues.title: §9.1 cites `TestMutationCheck` as the pinned mutation demo; no such class exists

The ceiling bullet was edited from "10 legs demoted, of which 7 ran on the baseline PR" to "9 legs demoted, of which 6 ran on the baseline PR" (correctly dropping sparq-py `arrow`), but the derived leg count on the last line of the same bullet was not updated: it still reads "Leg count 58 → 51 + 1–2 check shards".

51 was 58 − 7. With 6 legs now demoted from the baseline set it should be 58 → 52. The runner-minute range "28–30 of the 130" is also unreviewed against the removal of the ~1-min sparq-py leg, though that one is within rounding.
issues.fix_hint: Update to "Leg count 58 → 52 + 1–2 check shards", and sanity-check the "28–30 of the 130 leg runner-minutes" figure now that it covers only the 6 sparq-engine legs (the text already says "6 sparq-engine legs at 248–349 s each" was reduced to "the 6 sparq-engine legs" — keeping the per-leg seconds would let a reader re-derive the range instead of taking it on trust).

verdict.summary:
Round 3 clears the round-2 blocker; one major fail-open persists as a class.

RESOLVED (verified, not taken on trust):
- Blocker (arrow demotion): sparq-py.yml no longer carries `tier: check` and is absent from the diff. Sweeping all fragments: 169 legs, 0 declare any tier, so invariant (1) cannot fire. I ran the real `cmd_enforce(legs)` (stub YAML loader; PyYAML absent here as in round 2) under BOTH the new and the pre-PR sanitizer: "OK: 169 legs checked, 0 violations", exit 0 both times — the detector change moves no leg's enforcement outcome. The design record now states the honest 0-demotion result (§2.1 "Clear (0)", §9 floor 0, §9.1 audit entry).
- Minor (vacuous regression test): `test_regression_cfgs_from_rsp_and_reason_sources` now drives `_make_crate` + `classify_leg` and is non-vacuous — under the pre-PR sanitizer both legs classify sensitive=False; under the new one, True.
- Nit (docstring): carve-outs now stated explicitly. Suite green: 54 tests OK.

STILL OPEN (major): the raw-string lookbehind was widened to `(?<![A-Za-z0-9_"\\'])`, fixing the exact round-2 repro (`"\r"`; the new `test_escaped_cr_...` pins it and goes red on the old regex). But it excludes only word chars, quote, backslash, apostrophe — any OTHER char before a trailing `r` still opens a phantom raw string. Repros at PR head: `let m = "mode r";` and `let m = "w/r";` followed by `#[cfg(not(feature = "quoted-triples"))]` each yield `_extract_cfg_expressions() == []`; `#[cfg(feature = "vector-r")]` before another cfg yields ONE mangled expression swallowing it. A Rust lexer finds 86 phantom openers across `crates/**/*.rs` — the SAME count round 2 reported, so the fix changed which triggers fire, not how many; e.g. `"http://ex/r"` at crates/sparq-fedplan/src/adaptive.rs:1542. Blast radius today is zero (no span overlaps a live `#[cfg(`), hence major not blocker — but it is still a silent erasure in the demotion direction, the one thing the docstring promises cannot happen.
